subject: Request: short SOC 2 summary + permission for Acme customer story
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Lee <kevin.lee@acmecorp.com>, marketing@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick SOC 2 blurb and permission for customer story

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the kickoff call yesterday — Acme is excited to feature Redwood in our customer spotlight next month. Our product marketing team needs a short, public-facing paragraph (1-2 sentences) we can include under the security section of the case study. We also want to verify we can link to your SOC 2 attestation in the footer.

Specifically:
- Can you provide a 1-2 sentence technical blurb about Redwood's SOC 2 Type II coverage we can quote?
- Do we have permission to include a link to your SOC 2 attestation or a one-pager?
- Any preferred wording to avoid implying certification (we will use "SOC 2 attestation" or "SOC 2 Type II report attestation" depending on guidance).

We're aiming to publish the case study on March 25, so a response by EOD March 5 would be ideal.

Thanks — Jane

--
Jane Doe
Senior Product Marketing Manager, Acme Corp

Kimberly / Laura — forwarding Acme's ask. They need a short public blurb and permission to link our SOC 2 materials in their customer story.

Quick context: Acme is in our pilot with Dedicated; marketing wants to include a security line. Legal cc (Kevin) was on the original thread but I haven't looped our legal team yet.

Can you:
- Draft a 1-2 sentence public blurb that is technically accurate but clearance-friendly?
- Confirm we can provide a publicly linkable one-pager or drive link (I think yes) and whether we prefer specific wording to avoid certification misconceptions.

I'd like to get back to them by EOD 3/5.

Thanks — Marcus

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: security-ops@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick SOC 2 blurb and permission for customer story

Thanks for the ping — happy to provide. Below is a proposed public blurb and notes. I'll attach the one-pager and a URL we can share. Legal reviewed standard wording last quarter and recommended this conservative phrasing.

Proposed public blurb (1 sentence):
"Redwood Inference undergoes annual independent SOC 2 Type II attestation covering security and availability controls; a summarized attestation one-pager is available on request or via the public link provided below."

Suggested alternative (short):
"Redwood Inference maintains SOC 2 Type II attestation for relevant security and availability controls."

Notes / guidance:
- Avoid words like "certified" which can be ambiguous. 
- It's fine to link to a summarized one-pager or an access-controlled report link; we generally prefer the one-pager for external marketing.
- Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_one_pager.pdf (public summary). I've also included a text file with the public link we've used for other case studies.

Permission: Approved to link to the one-pager or include the one-sentence blurb above. If Acme wants verbatim language in their hero line, we recommend the first proposed sentence.

Happy to tweak if Laura wants any marketing polish.

Kimberly Park
Senior Security Manager | Redwood Inference

Hi Jane — thanks for the request and for flagging the publish date.

Kimberly approved the wording and we're happy for Acme to use the short blurb below in the customer story:

"Redwood Inference undergoes annual independent SOC 2 Type II attestation covering security and availability controls; a summarized attestation one-pager is available on request or via the public link provided."

We also give Acme permission to include a link to the Redwood SOC 2 one-pager. I've attached the PDF (Redwood_SOC2_one_pager.pdf) and included the public link in the related_links field in case you need it for the draft.

If you need a slightly shorter variant for a sidebar, use: "Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II attestation for security and availability."

Please let me know if your legal team wants any additional guardrails; happy to loop in our legal folks.

Best — Marcus
